- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true peak); apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out post-spike forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecasts are 10%+ above or below recent 5-day average, adjust toward historical mean (last 10–15 days) unless sentiment overrides.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in early period (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; increase early forecast values by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to forecast decline onset.
